'''Koyasu Jizō-ji''' (子安地蔵寺) is a {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|qid=Q5393308|lt=Shingon Buddhist temple}} of the {{ill|Kōyasan Shingon-shū|fr|Kōyasan Shingon-shū|ja|高野山真言宗|zh|高野山真言宗|qid=Q3077357|lt=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} sect, located in {{ill|Hashimoto, Wakayama|ja|和歌山県橋本市|qid=Q842098}}. Its {{ill|sangō|ja|山号|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11058522}} is *Isan-zan* (易産山), and its principal image is {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|bg|Кшитигарбха|bn|ক্ষিতিগর্ভ|bo|ས་ཡི་སྙིང་པོ།|ca|Ksitigarbha|cs|Kšitigarbha|de|Kshitigarbha|el|Τζίζο|eo|Kŝitigarbo|es|Ksitigarbha|fa|کشیتی‌گربه|fr|Kshitigarbha|hu|Dzsizó|id|Kṣitigarbha|it|Kṣitigarbha|ja|地蔵菩薩|ka|ქშიტიგარბჰა|km|ក្សិតិគភ៌|ko|지장보살|mk|Џизо Бозацу|nl|Ksitigarbha|pl|Ksitigarbha|pt|Dizang|ro|Ksitigarbha|ru|Кшитигарбха|simple|Kṣitigarbha|sv|Ksitigarbha|ta|இக்சிதிகர்பர்|th|พระกษิติครรภโพธิสัตว์|tr|Ksitigarbha|uk|Кшітіґарбга|vi|Địa Tạng|wuu|地藏菩萨|zh|地藏菩萨|zh_min_nan|Tē-chōng-phô͘-sat|zh_yue|地藏菩薩|qid=Q604687|lt=Jizō Bosatsu}}. The temple’s formal name is *Isan-zan Gokoku-in Jizō-ji* (易産山護国院地蔵寺), while *Koyasu Jizō-ji* is a commonly used name. It is well known for its wisteria flowers.

(승려)|pl|Gyōki|ru|Гёки|zh|行基|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}}. The temple’s principal image, a statue of {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|bg|Кшитигарбха|bn|ক্ষিতিগর্ভ|bo|ས་ཡི་སྙིང་པོ།|ca|Ksitigarbha|cs|Kšitigarbha|de|Kshitigarbha|el|Τζίζο|eo|Kŝitigarbo|es|Ksitigarbha|fa|کشیتی‌گربه|fr|Kshitigarbha|hu|Dzsizó|id|Kṣitigarbha|it|Kṣitigarbha|ja|地蔵菩薩|ka|ქშიტიგარბჰა|km|ក្សិតិគភ៌|ko|지장보살|mk|Џизо Бозацу|nl|Ksitigarbha|pl|Ksitigarbha|pt|Dizang|ro|Ksitigarbha|ru|Кшитигарбха|simple|Kṣitigarbha|sv|Ksitigarbha|ta|இக்சிதிகர்பர்|th|พระกษิติครรภโพธิสัตว์|tr|Ksitigarbha|uk|Кшітіґарбга|vi|Địa Tạng|wuu|地藏菩萨|zh|地藏菩萨|zh_min_nan|Tē-chōng-phô͘-sat|zh_yue|地藏菩薩|qid=Q604687|lt=Jizō Bosatsu}}, is said to have been carved by Gyōki himself and is known as the "Most Victorious and Oldest Jizō Bosatsu in Japan." This Jizō was enshrined at the temple to provide prayers for safe childbirth, leading to its name *Koyasu Jizō* (子安地蔵).<ref name="temple_history">[https://hananotera.com/history History of Koyasu Jizō-ji]</ref>

In {{ill|1581|ja|天正9年|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506281}} ({{ill|1581|en|1581|qid=Q6717|lt=1581 AD}}), during the {{ill|Kōyasan Campaign|ja|高野山攻め|qid=Q140446052}} led by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}} and his son {{ill|Oda Nobutaka|en|Oda Nobutaka|qid=Q2614349|lt=Oda Nobutaka}}, the temple was set ablaze, and all its structures were destroyed. However, the principal image was hidden deep in the mountains and later discovered by villagers. The location where it was hidden is still known today as *Kakuregata* (かくれがた).<ref name="temple_history"/>

During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the temple gained significant patronage from {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|en|Tokugawa Yorinobu|qid=Q1045763|lt=Tokugawa Yorinobu}}, lord of the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}}, after it was said to have helped his daughter through a difficult childbirth. Koyasu Jizō-ji subsequently became the official prayer temple for safe childbirth for the {{ill|Kishū Tokugawa family|en|Kishū Tokugawa family|qid=Q11605046|lt=Kishū Tokugawa family}}. In {{ill|1645|ja|正保2年|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506284}} ({{ill|1645|en|1645|qid=Q6925|lt=1645 AD}}), the temple was designated as a branch temple under {{ill|Takashitsu-in Temple|ja|高室院|qid=Q135506286}} on {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|qid=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya}}, overseeing 11 sub-temples in the present-day Hashimoto area. Another temple was added to its jurisdiction in {{ill|1784|ja|天明4年|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506287}} ({{ill|1784|en|1784|qid=Q7752|lt=1784 AD}}).<ref name="temple_history"/>

In {{ill|1648|ja|正保5年|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506289}} ({{ill|1648|en|1648|qid=Q6941|lt=1648 AD}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|en|Tokugawa Yorinobu|qid=Q1045763|lt=Tokugawa Yorinobu}} restored the temple buildings.<ref name="temple_history"/> He also granted the temple 2 *chōbu* (町歩) of farmland to cover the costs of worship and offerings for the principal image. Yorinobu visited the temple 11 times, and from then on, successive lords of the Kishū Domain and their retainers made frequent pilgrimages.<ref name="temple_history"/>

== Temple Grounds ==

* Main Hall (本堂)
* Kuri (庫裏) - Temple living quarters
* Mizuko Jizō Hall (水子地蔵堂)
* Bell Tower (鐘楼)
* Wisteria Garden (藤の庭)
* Mountain Gate (山門) - Two-story Nagaya-mon (長屋門)
